contexts.text: A principle from which he is never willing to recede, or in the least to let go.
If the Lord were to relax in the least... the man would do evil... AC 929:end.
Therefore man ought not to hang down his hands. AC 1937:2. AC 8176. AC 10299:4. DP 210. TCR 356. SE 2161. SE 2732.
The Angels are remitted into their evils. AC 2307. AC 4564:3. HH 342.
They are first remitted into the life which they had in the world.
Truths are successively remitted from within.
Relieve sins are remitted in a moment.
They are told that the Lord remits the sins of everyone who from his heart desires it; but still such persons are nut separated from the diabolical crew...
They think that (in that case) they would hang down their lands...
Like objects which do not remit, but absorb the rays of light.
With the Jews it was implanted that they should never forgive...
Forgive the transgression of thy brethren () = supplication and repentance.
For they are remiss () = not sufficiently infested. AC 7149.
Forgive... my sin, this time only () = that they should not regard his disobedience... For to remit is to regard one, not from evil, but from good.
Those in temptations are wont to hang down their hands.
As he hangs down his hands, he yields...
Under Repent, see this reference. AC 8393.
The Angels are remitted into the state of the natural affections... AC 8487:3.
The concupiscences into which (the Angels) are remitted, are...
The Lord continually remits...
They are then remitted into the evils of their will.

All sin... shall be forgiven unto men; but the blasphemy of the Spirit shall not be forgiven... A word against the Son of Man shall be forgiven; but he who shall speak against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven... ()... = the profanation of truth... (This) cannot be healed, thus not forgiven... AC 8883.

The reason these are not forgiven, is that hypocrisy... infects the interiors... For the forgiveness (or remission) of sins is the separation of evil from good... which cannot be done with one with whom all good is destroyed...
Damnation although he... supplicates for forgiveness... Signified, Explained.
Deceit in spiritual things... cannot be forgiven. Explained.
When such supplicate for forgiveness... they supplicate nothing from the heart... Hence they have no forgiveness.

The remission (or forgiveness) of sins (is supposed to be) the wiping of them away... and that after the remission they go clean... but the case is quite different with the remission of sins. The Lord remits sins to everyone... but they are not on that account remitted, unless the man performs serious repentance, and desists from evils, and then lives a life of faith and charity, and this up to the end of his life. When he does this, he receives new spiritual life from the Lord, and when from this life he regards the evils of his former life, and feels aversion and horror for them, then, first, are the evils remitted; for the man is then kept in truths and goods by the Lord, and is withheld from evils. Hence it is evident what is the remission of sins, and that this cannot exist within an hour, or within a year. This is known by the Church, for it is said to those who approach the Holy Supper that their sins are remitted if they begin a new life...
That this malignity is not remitted, because it is against the Divine justice. Signified, Explained.
The case with the remission of sins is that man is not purified from them, but is withheld from them by the Lord... when he has been regenerated. Explained. AC 9447, Explained. AC 9448.
(The doctrine) of the remission of sins. General article. NJHD 159.
That no one can lead away from sins, thus remit them, except the Lord. Signified.
The ability to be kept by the Lord in the good of love and truths of faith, and to be withheld from evils and falsities, is the remission of sins. (Possible only to the regenerate.)
The signs that sins have been remitted are as follow. Enumerated.
The signs that sins have not been remitted. Enumerated.
Sins, when remitted... remain with the man.
These are the things which are meant by the remission of sins from mercy. Enumerated.
From these things it is evident who they are whose sins have been remitted, and who those whose sins are not remitted.
The mercy-seat = the cleansing from evils or remission of sins. Explained.
Hence it is said that this sin (against the Holy Spirit, which is profanation) cannot be forgiven.
For deliverance from sins, or the remission of them, is nothing else than removal; for they remain with the man...
If now Thou remittest their sin () = that this turning away from the Divine would not oppose.
What is not attended to, is said to be remitted.
In this second state (after death) they are remitted... into the state of their exteriors...
That the imputation of the Lord's merit is nothing else than the remission of sins after repentance. General article.
The remission of sins as preached, and as described by the Lord. Illustrated. DLord 18:5.
Being ready to forgive others... as ye would have forgiveness of your offences of God's hand. (Quotation from the English in this no.) (Translated into Latin in 6. TCR 526:2.)
The Holy Supper confirms the remission of sins with those who perform repentance. Explained.
That in proportion as evils are removed, they are remitted. General article.
I had believed that when evils are remitted, they are rejected... But all things remain, and when, after repentance, they are remitted, they are moved away from the middle to the sides...
Some good men after death... glory because they are no longer sinners... and are therefore remitted into their own evils...

That sins when remitted have been removed, is an error of the age. (Such) believe that sins are remitted them through the (Holy) Supper... and through faith alone, etc... But the reverse is true: that when sins have been removed they are remitted; for repentance precedes remission, and without repentance there is no remission. Therefore the Lord commanded the disciples to preach repentance for the remission of sins (); and John preached the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins (). The Lord remits their sins to all... but still He cannot take them away except according to the laws of His Divine Providence. (It was He who said to Peter) that he should forgive his brother seventy times seven ().
They are remitted to such (as are in like delight).
This is meant by the good measure... given into the bosom of those who forgive and give to others (); that is, who are in the good of charity.
In proportion as he does this, his sins are remitted.
Provided the priest says, I remit.
God cannot according to His laws remit sins to any man, except in proportion as the man according to His laws desists from them.
That the Divine virtue and operation... is, according to these... remission of sins. Explained.
Purification from evils is the remission of sins.
I have heard from Heaven that the Lord remits everyone his sins... but that still sins are not wiped away thereby, but only by repentance.
They are remitted to those who instruct...
He said, Charity is to forgive everyone his trespasses.
In proportion as man performs repentance, sins are removed with him; and in proportion as these are removed, in the same proportion they are remitted.

There is no need to supplicate before the Lord for the remission of sins... First, because sins are not abolished, but removed, and they are removed in proportion as the man desists from them... Secondly, because the Lord... remits his sins to everyone...
Every man after death... is first remitted into his externals.
That in proportion as man is regenerated, his sins are removed, and that this removal is the remission of sins. General article.
(Thus) the remission of sins is not their extirpation and wiping away, but their removal and separation...
(Thus) the remission of sins is not instantaneous, but follows regeneration, according to the progress of it. The removal of sins, which is called their remission, may be compared to...
They are remitted into the Heaven of Spirits.
Represented by the remission of their endeavours.
It was remitted them for a while... SE 2801.
When it is remitted them, they at once rush...
This bond is remitted...
Others complained that they were remitted.
Thus do Spirits abhor the remission of bonds.
All, even Angels, can be remitted into the same state as they had possessed in the life of the body; so that if the human race were to fail, Spirits could be remitted into a like state...
That the Lord should not remit His Divine force. Signified.
When such Spirits are remitted...
When they are remitted into a state like that of their life in the body...
(or SE 3116). He no longer desires that it may be remitted to him to fall into his delights.
As if they were remitted from the world of this sun...
Sins are not remitted unless confessed from the heart, with a certain inward torture...
Spirits are not remitted into any other life than that which they have acquired by actuality. Explained.
As to infants, who are remitted into a life not acquired by actuality...
Remit sins by the papal bulls.
They would drag him, if he slackened.
They are remitted into their delights...
She was remitted into thoughts such as she had had in the body.
They suppose they can sin, because after some time they have instantaneous remission.
All are by degrees remitted into the life they had had in the world...
He contaminated Divine things by... praying devoutly for forgiveness...
(In England) there is no remission (of penalties).
He said that his sins are remitted because he holds their faith; and that if he does not desist, they are still remitted, but not in the same degree.
To forgive seven times = to forgive as often as [the offender] should... say that he repented, thus at all times. AE 391:20.
The remission of its influx. Signified, Explained. AE 419.
As charity towards the neighbour is meant, it is said, Forgive and it shall be forgiven unto you ().
He who hangs down his hands, and awaits influx, receives nothing...
That to deny the Word is the sin which cannot be forgiven. Explained.
This soul shall be utterly cut off, its iniquity is upon it = that it cannot be forgiven. Explained.
(Thus) those who hang down their hands... remain in the state of their evil; and hang down their hands to eternity.
Fr. G. prayed to God the Father with most ardent fervour, believing that when he did this, all things were remitted...
They who confirm themselves that all evils are remitted by the Holy Supper (merely), have adultery with a maternal aunt.

Holy Spirit. 5. 8. That to him who speaks a word against the Holy Spirit it is not remitted, is because he denies the Divinity of the Lord and the holiness of the Word; for such a one has no religion. See also CanonsNC 9.
